name: tag
purpose: Compact status or category label with severity-based color coding. Supports optional icon, pill shape via `rounded`, and two sizes aligned with the Webkit Figma Tag component set.
useWhen: Label or categorize an item with a short descriptive text, optionally with a leading icon or pill shape.
Show a status/category with severity color via `severity`.

Mark the one value a list highlights (the Owner role in a users table) with `severity="highlight"`: the brand orange as a tint, orange text on `--primary-mask`, like the success, info and warning tints.
avoidWhen: It is purely a count or one-glance status label → use `badge`.
The user can select or remove it (filters, multi-select values) → use `chip`.
related: badge` — denser count/short-label indicator with no icon affordance.
bestPractices: Severity comes from `severity`; the optional icon is decorative — keep it `aria-hidden`.

Pick the severity by meaning: `success` Active, `warning` Pending, `secondary` Inactive or a neutral category (Developer, Viewer), `info` a second role (Admin), `highlight` the one value to single out (Owner), `primary` a solid brand label. Do not use `danger` for a state that is only off (Inactive): it reads as an error.
Do not restyle a Tag with colour classes to get a tint; every tint is a `severity`.
Use `rounded` for the pill shape rather than a custom radius.

props.name: label
props.doc: Fallback text when the default slot is empty.

props.name: severity
props.doc: Color style for the tag surface and label; `primary` is solid brand orange, `highlight` the brand orange as a tint, `contrast` uses `var(--bg-contrast)` / `var(--text-contrast)`.

props.name: icon
props.doc: PrimeIcons class for the leading icon.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'
</script>

<template>
  <Tag
    label="Label"
    severity="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
